## Case studies

Each card on the homepage links to a decision record in the planet-express
repo. Status is stated on the card. The three delivered ones are also published
as FAQPage structured data on the homepage, so an answer engine can quote them
and cite the ADR.

- [Why Talos, not k3s (ADR-001)](https://github.com/geripgeri/planet-express/blob/main/docs/decisions/ADR-001-kubernetes.md): delivered. Minimal, immutable, API-managed nodes, provisioned by OpenTofu. No SSH, no shell, no package manager, so the whole node is defined in git. k3s makes setup faster by bundling components and relaxing defaults, which suits getting started but not a system meant to mirror production.
- [One public repo, no home network (ADR-021)](https://github.com/geripgeri/planet-express/blob/main/docs/decisions/ADR-021-public-mirror-privacy-partitioning.md): delivered. A mirror workflow reads export-ignore paths from .gitattributes and strips them from the published history, then gitleaks scans what is left. It aborts rather than publish if the exclusion list comes back empty.
- [Secrets you can still read in review (ADR-009)](https://github.com/geripgeri/planet-express/blob/main/docs/decisions/ADR-009-sops.md): delivered. SOPS with age encrypts values and leaves YAML field names in plaintext, so a secret change reads as a one-line diff instead of an opaque blob. Kubernetes Secrets are decrypted inside the ArgoCD repo-server by ksops.
- [Paging through Signal (ADR-012)](https://github.com/geripgeri/planet-express/blob/main/docs/decisions/ADR-012-alerting.md): in progress, the decision record exists but implementation is not complete. The planned design routes Alertmanager to Signal, which pushes to my phone. Email waits until I open my inbox, which is wrong for a page.
- [All decision records](https://github.com/geripgeri/planet-express/tree/main/docs/decisions): the full set

## Current work

I lead Cloud Infrastructure at Protex AI. I set technical direction, review
important pull requests, and write infrastructure code every week.

When the Infrastructure Team was formed in May 2026, I decided to step back
from people management and returned to a hands-on Lead DevOps Engineer role.

- I lead infrastructure incident response and post-mortems, and I am the go-to person for infrastructure issues

Engineering Manager and Lead DevOps Engineer, Cloud Infrastructure Team,
September 2025 to May 2026:

- I built a cross-country engineering team from zero, including 1:1s, status cadences, coaching, and team operations

I work best in a player-coach role, combining technical direction,
mentoring, and hands-on infrastructure engineering.

## Notes

- This file follows the llms.txt convention: an H1, a summary, then linked
  sections. Every link is a real URL, on this site or on GitHub.
- This site is one static HTML page. No trackers, no analytics.
- All profile content is in the served HTML, not rendered by JavaScript, so
  nothing here is hidden behind a script that a crawler might not run.
- Page freshness: the JSON-LD dateModified and the sitemap lastmod are bumped
  by CI on every merged pull request.
